limitations: Independent agent walkthrough in headless Chromium by a different agent from the author and the source reviewer; not a human user study and not feature-owner approval.

The lab openlaw-docs-80ceef9e-work2 (work2) is shared with other DOC-030 walkthrough agents. This run created only records named "DOC-030 entities ..." (run tag 0925-1129), plus records from earlier development runs of the same script with other tags. API calls prepared fixtures or read back results the browser had already shown; every documented action ran through the browser controls.

Author limitation, checked on the lab: V-C32 asks to record a Holding. On an Entity that keeps a share register the owner Holdings come from Register entries; the walkthrough should record the Holding on an Entity without a register, or as an owned Entity, and use the share register (entity-structure-and-access) for register-backed owners.
Author limitation, checked on the lab: Hand-typed owners can still be added to an Entity that keeps a register (see productBugs). The guide describes that behaviour and recommends a register entry.

3 page loads showed the app's "Something went wrong." screen with net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED while other labs changed the host's Docker networks; the script reloaded once and the step then passed. This is an environment effect, not an app finding.
The out-of-range Holding percentage refusal shows the generic "One or more request fields are invalid."; the article quotes no message.

The paragraphs about register-derived rows (From register, a register entry replacing a hand-typed Entity owner, a hand-typed individual staying beside the register Holder, and a hand-typed owner still accepted on a register Entity) were walked on the lab in the V-C53 run of entity-structure-and-access (same log). They behaved as this article says. The acceptance of a hand-typed owner on a register Entity is recorded as a product bug in the log.
Not exercised: adding an Officer role (Administrator settings on a shared lab) and a concurrent archive or restore by another person.
